notes.markdown:
Release 1.1: messaging on a par with the best chat apps, group video rooms with screen sharing on every device, sign-in on as many devices as you like, self-service password reset, a rebuilt push-to-talk, and new tools for automations, managed-service providers and AI oversight.

## New

- **Messaging, rebuilt.** Chat in MonoPhone now works the way people expect from their favourite messenger. You see when the other person is typing and when they were last online, in the chat header and in the Messages list. Ticks show sent, delivered and read; in a group a message counts as read only when everyone has read it, and Info on your own message lists when each member received and read it. Search finds message text, not only chat names. The web console chat shows typing, last seen and message info too (iPhone, Android, web console).
- **Albums, offline media and a richer composer.** Photos and videos sent together appear as one album. Photos, videos, voice notes and files wait on the phone while you are offline and send themselves when you are back, never twice. Replies in a one-to-one chat appear as quotes in the conversation, Edit is one tap away, and the reaction bar opens every emoji, with categories, search in nine languages and your recent emoji. Share a contact, start a video call from a one-to-one chat, and keep a draft's reply and mentions (iPhone, Android).
- **Clearer group chats.** Groups show who created the group, who joined, left or was added, and the members' names under the group's name; a new group starts by picking people (iPhone, Android, web console).
- **Group video rooms that hold up.** Rooms with several people (tested with five: tablets, phones and browsers together) now show every member once, in a named tile, and keep working through a network change, a held call or a member who joins from two devices. Any member can add another person to the room. In a group video call the browser phone in the web console now receives everyone's video too. A video call or room shows live captions, and a refused recording is explained in your language (iPhone, Android, Mac, Windows, web console).
- **Screen sharing everywhere, including iPhone and iPad.** Share screen sits beside Hang up on every MonoPhone, now also on iPhone and iPad (stop it from the red status-bar pill or Control Center), and the web console can share a browser tab, window or screen in one-to-one calls and video rooms. A shared screen gets the large tile in a room (iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, Windows, web console).
- **Sign in on all your devices.** Signing in on a new phone, computer or browser never signs out or disconnects the ones you already use; calls ring on all of them. A set-up code for a device that is already in use now adds a new device instead of taking that one over. See the note under Improved about the sign-in limit.
- **Forgot password?** Users can reset their own password from the console sign-in page and from MonoPhone: they receive an e-mail with a link and an eight-digit code, valid for 30 minutes and usable once. The answer never reveals whether an account exists, the number of requests is limited, and a reset signs the account out everywhere. Accounts that sign in with single sign-on are told to use it instead. Requires outgoing e-mail to be set up on the PBX.
- **Push-to-talk, redesigned.** The channel page works like a radio: who is online updates at once, your own row says You, the big button shows who is talking and cannot be pressed while someone else talks (a supervisor can hold to take over), and notification and key settings moved into a channel settings sheet. Talking is shown in the accent colour and listening in blue on the phone, the widgets, Control Center and Apple Watch (iPhone, Android, Apple Watch, Wear OS).
- **End-to-end encrypted chat.** A one-to-one chat can be encrypted so that only the two phones can read it: open the chat's menu, choose Turn on end-to-end encryption, and compare or scan the security code with the other person. Encryption survives app restarts, the chat shows when it is being set up and when someone's security code changes, and replies keep their quote. Group chats, calls, search, AI features and attachments are not covered yet, and it cannot be turned off for that chat. An administrator allows or blocks it (Admin, Settings, Company, Chat controls) (iPhone, Android).
- **Group video tile grid.** On a video call with more than two people, MonoPhone and the browser phone in the web console show everyone in a grid with names, a ring around whoever is speaking, and a photo or initials when someone's camera is off. In MonoPhone you can drag your own picture to any corner, and it never covers a name. The earlier note about multi-party video calls described this feature before it was fully in place; it works as described from this release.
- **Video rooms for guests: screen sharing, recording and captions.** Anyone in a room can share their screen. The host can record the meeting, and everyone sees a clear banner while it records (the recording is kept for your company's usual retention period). Live captions can be turned on in a room, off by default; each person chooses whether their own speech is captioned. A room holds up to 12 people, a limit based on a measured load test (Admin, Settings, Telephony, Video).
- **Copilot everywhere.** Ask Copilot from the search bar of the web console (Ctrl+K or Cmd+K) and from a new icon in MonoPhone. It sees and changes only what you could yourself: users get answers about their own calls, supervisors about their team, administrators about the whole company. The icon appears only when your company's AI is on (iPhone, Android, Mac, Windows).
- **SMPP server for messaging partners.** A partner's messaging system can now connect to MonoPbx over SMPP to send and receive text messages on your numbers, with per-partner logins, address allow-lists, rate and daily limits, optional TLS, and a live view of which partners are connected. A partner can keep several connections open at once (up to 4 by default, at most 10), and messages are spread over the least busy one. Messages they send follow the usual STOP and blocklist rules and can start an automation (Admin, Messaging, SMS).
- **Move a company between installations.** Partners can export one company's configuration to an encrypted file and import it as a new company on another installation, from the partner portal (Export a company in the company menu, and Import a company) or with the `mpbx` command-line tool. An import is always checked first and shows what it will create, what conflicts and which credentials must be entered again, before a separate Apply step. With the command-line tool, call history, and recordings, voicemail and fax files, can be included for companies not under a legal hold.
- **Turn any call into a video conference.** In MonoPhone, More, Video conference moves the call you are on, including one with a person on an ordinary phone line, into a video conference, and Back to audio call returns. The browser phone in the web console has the same button in its More menu. Automations get a matching step (iPhone, Android, Mac, Windows, web console).
- **Add participant.** On a call, pick colleagues by name or extension, or type a number. People are rung in turn and joined automatically when they answer, and you can see who is on the call and remove someone (iPhone, Android, Mac, Windows).
- **Picture-in-picture for video calls.** Leave MonoPhone during a video call and the other person's picture keeps floating over your other apps (iPhone, Android).
- **Active speaker settings.** Administrators can tune how loud someone has to be to count as speaking, and how long the highlight stays (Admin, Settings, Telephony, Video).
- **My follow-ups.** A new Follow-ups page in the web console and a list in the app show the promises you made on calls: overdue, due today, upcoming. Mark one done or snooze it; supervisors see a read-only My team tab. Reminders on iPhone have Done and Snooze buttons, and Android has its own notification channel.
- **Chat media composer.** Photos and videos open in a full-screen preview where you can add more shots, remove items and trim a video before sending. Locations are small map bubbles, with one-tap send of your position, and live location can be shared for 15 minutes, 1 hour or 8 hours. A Shared tab shows thumbnails, file icons, playable voice notes and link previews (iPhone, Android).
- **AI governance and activity ledger.** One page shows what every AI feature actually did: the voice agent, chat assist, the admin copilot, automation AI steps, connected AI assistants and captions and summaries. Switch each AI surface on or off, limit the tools it may use, and optionally store the text (off by default, with retention and redaction settings). The ledger records what was done, never the prompt or answer unless you choose to store it (Admin, AI, AI agents, AI governance).
- **Fully private AI.** A mode that keeps AI inside your own network: while it is on, AI features can only use language and speech providers on a list of private servers approved by the person who runs the installation, and a verification report shows what was checked. MonoPhone prefers on-device AI in this mode (Admin, AI, Fully private AI).
- **Call path analyzer.** See where callers of a call flow go: which menu options they press, where they give up, and where calls fail, with sample calls behind each number (Admin, Call handling, Call flows, Call path analyzer).
- **Registration health.** A live view of which extensions are registered, on which phone or app, and whether the busy lamps on desk phones are being kept up to date. A new alert tells you when watched extensions go offline (Admin, Monitoring and reports, Registration health).
- **Database step and data tables for automations.** Look a caller up in your own PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB or SQL Server database, using a saved credential, with read-only access by default. Data tables are small spreadsheets your automations can read and write (call-back lists, VIP numbers), with CSV import and export (Admin, Call handling, Call flows, Data tables).
- **Seven new call-flow steps.** The flow builder gains seven new steps, plus regex, date and sum transforms, and every step now offers all of its options in the editor. Appointment and payment reminders arrive as five ready-made templates in the template gallery.
- **More automation steps: files, Google Workspace and parcels.** Read or save a file in your own Amazon S3, S3-compatible or Google Cloud Storage bucket using a saved credential. Send an e-mail, search Drive or save a file to Drive as a chosen user with a connected Google account. Watch a DHL, Estafeta or FedEx shipment by tracking number (shipments of marketplace orders are watched automatically) and start an automation when its status changes.
- **Export and import call flows.** Export a flow, with the flows it calls and its data tables, as one file and import it into another company or installation. Integrations, saved credentials, queues, numbers and other things a flow refers to are matched by name and reported before you apply, and an imported flow is never published automatically (Admin, Call handling, Call flows: Export on the flow list, and Import a flow).
- **Copilot and AI assistants can build automations.** The admin Copilot can now draft and edit call flows and automations as change sets you review before applying, and AI assistants connected over MCP get matching tools to build, check, test and publish flows. Nothing is published without an explicit step.
- **PayPal payment links.** Send a PayPal payment link from a flow or an AI assistant and check the payment's status (Admin, Settings, Integrations).
- **Jira steps for automations.** Create a Jira issue or add a comment from a flow, using the company's Jira connection (Admin, Jira).
- **Salesforce, HubSpot and Pipedrive in automations.** These three CRMs can now be installed as integrations, so automations and AI agents can look up a caller and create contacts and notes in them (Admin, Settings, Integrations).
- **Company key-value store for automations.** Three new steps keep and read small values (a counter, a last-seen date, a flag) across runs without setting up a table.
- **Report ad conversions from a flow.** A flow can report a call as a Google Ads or Meta Ads conversion, using the same attribution and minimum talk-time rules as the automatic upload, and tells you why when nothing was sent.
- **ConnectWise Manage and Autotask for managed-service providers.** The caller card shows the caller's company and open tickets, missed calls and voicemails can open a service ticket, and the partner portal can import PSA customers as client companies and export monthly usage per client (Admin, Settings, Integrations).
- **Number reputation checks.** Look up whether a number is valid, its line type and carrier, and (with Twilio) a fraud-risk score, using your own Twilio Lookup or Numverify account. Use the answer in a flow, from an outbound-number monitor, or from a connected AI assistant (Admin, Settings, Integrations).
- **Integration status.** Each integration now shows how far it has been checked against a real vendor account, and a new documentation page lists the status of every connector.
- **Customer offboarding wizard for partners.** Hand a client company over in five steps: revoke devices, release numbers or mark them for port-out, record a final usage bill, and more. Each step is remembered and audited, nothing is ever deleted, and a legal hold blocks company deletion (Admin, Settings, System, Companies, Partners).
- **MonoPhone for Mac updates itself.** The Mac app checks for updates daily and from Check for Updates in the app menu, the menu bar icon and Settings, shows what changed, and installs verified updates. Companies can turn it off with a device-management profile. The Mac app is now a signed, notarized drag-to-install disk image (Mac).
- **Browser extension for Firefox.** Click-to-dial, the caller card and the phone panel (in the sidebar) now work in Firefox 140 or later, matching Chrome and Edge. Firefox for Android is not supported (Firefox).
- **Message from your iPhone contacts.** On iPhone, Message on a contact card now offers MonoPhone, and you can ask Siri to send a message with MonoPhone (iPhone).

## Improved

- **Please note: sign-in limit.** When a user reaches the maximum number of signed-in devices, a new sign-in is now refused with a clear message instead of silently signing out their oldest device. The default limit is now 100 devices per user, and only devices used recently count. Users can sign out old devices from My devices.
- **Please note: update the PBX for the newest app features.** Typing and last seen, per-member message info times, encrypted-chat quotes, the improved video rooms and Forgot password need this PBX release. Newer MonoPhone apps keep working for calls and chat with an older PBX.
- Too many devices on a line: MonoPhone and the web console now say so plainly, explain that each installation counts as a device, and offer Remove an old device, after which the line connects (iPhone, Android, Mac, Windows, web console).
- Recents in MonoPhone now combines this phone's own calls with the company call history, so a call missed seconds ago is always listed and counted, even when the history cannot be loaded. Names come from your contacts and the company phonebook, each day is shown once, and times use one format.
- MonoPhone looks and feels more native on iPhone: system alerts, action sheets and menus, destructive actions in red, one empty-state style, coloured icon tiles on the Me page, clearer settings pages, and permission screens that explain each permission before the system asks for it, instead of a notification prompt right after sign-in.
- MonoPhone on Android supports predictive back and a per-app language, uses Android wording in its settings, keeps live Quick Settings tiles and widget previews up to date, and goes Up to the right page after opening from a widget, tile or shortcut.
- MonoPhone stays readable at large text sizes: the keypad fits above the tab bar on small phones, words and numbers no longer break mid-word, and Sign in stays reachable with the keyboard open on small phones.
- When push notifications are not working, MonoPhone shows an amber notice that calls ring only while the app is open, instead of a general error (Android).
- The call screen shows when the other side has put you on hold, offers only the controls that work while a call is ringing, explains when a video call has no camera, and shows a colleague's name instead of their extension.
- Push-to-talk is more reliable: it notices a lost connection, reconnects at once when the network returns, rejoins your last channel after a restart, and keeps the last words of a transmission on Android.
- Push-to-talk tells you when you are talking on your other device instead of dropping the audio silently.
- Every page of the help documentation is now translated and kept current in all nine languages, and translated pages link correctly to their sections.
- Automations that start from an integration event now cover more kinds of connectors, including ticketing, accounting, e-commerce, meetings and messaging. Orders from Amazon Mexico, Liverpool and Coppel are checked every 15 minutes and start those automations too.
- The SMPP server can use a chosen certificate, reloads it without a restart, and checks that partner connections are still alive.
- Notion gets a tool to append text to a page, usable from flows and AI assistants.
- The automation "send webhook" step is now described as the way to trigger Zapier, Make and n8n.
- A server address typed with the plain (non-secure) scheme in MonoPhone is now kept instead of silently switched to the secure one, with a clear warning on plain connections and the exact address named when it cannot be reached. An address typed without any scheme always uses the secure one (iPhone, Android, Mac, Windows).
- Sending the onboarding invitation to a new device is much faster.
- The call-flow designer can go full screen (a button in the zoom bar, or Ctrl or Cmd plus Shift plus F), and remembers your choice in that browser.
- The automation "send SMS" step can send an MMS with picture or video links, on providers that support it (Twilio today).
- The automation "post to Microsoft Teams" step posts to the channels of your Microsoft Teams integration.
- The payment-link step lists only the payment connectors you have installed.
- Automations can now start from an integration event only for a chosen record, for example a single order, using a field filter on the event.
- The "add a note to the CRM" automation step no longer offers professional-services (PSA) and accounting connectors as if they were CRMs.
- The automation "send email" step can set a reply-to address, so replies go to a person or shared mailbox instead of the sending address.
- Maps follow the platform: Apple Watch shows Apple Maps, Android and Wear OS show Google Maps.
- Video calls now prefer the more widely compatible video format, the same order audio already used.
- When someone turns their camera off, their picture is replaced by their photo or initials and name.
- The MonoPhone menu bar icon menu on the Mac is reorganized and shows the current version.
- An SMS whose delivery result is unclear is now looked up before it is sent again.
- On iPhone your own camera stays on in picture-in-picture during a video call or room, so the others still see you while you use another app, and your own picture appears in a small inset (iPhone).
- Video rooms name every colleague on the tiles and in the room list, also in the web console when the colleague was dialled by number, and the web console's call header follows who is still in the room.
- Add person in a video room no longer puts the room on hold while the new person's phone rings. When they cannot be reached, the room comes back at once and MonoPhone says why: busy, declined, cannot be reached, no answer, not found or not allowed (iPhone, Android).
- German texts on Apple Watch and Wear OS now use the formal address like the rest of MonoPhone, and Spanish (Mexico) and Italian texts in the console, MonoPhone and the help documentation consistently use the informal address.
- The integration status page now also lists HubSpot, Pipedrive, Salesforce, Numverify and Twilio Lookup, and eight help pages that could only be reached by a link now appear in the documentation menu.

## Fixed

- Fixed attended transfer in MonoPhone: Transfer to your other call now works, and the transferred caller keeps their audio.
- Fixed calling back from Recents or a contact card on iPhone, which did not place the call (iPhone).
- Fixed push-to-talk being silent right after a voice or video call (iPhone, Android).
- Fixed links from widgets, Quick Settings tiles, launcher shortcuts and app actions doing nothing on Android, including the push-to-talk tile (Android).
- Fixed screen sharing crashing MonoPhone on Android 14 and later (Android).
- Fixed the camera freezing when MonoPhone moved to the background during a video call; it now pauses and resumes (iPhone, Android).
- Fixed chat problems: words typed while a message was being sent were lost, a chat left open in the background marked messages as read, a failed message disappeared instead of offering a retry, a deleted message came back while offline, the unread divider stayed put, and tapping a quote of an older message did nothing.
- Fixed a message written offline showing the time it was finally sent instead of the time it was written.
- Fixed an encrypted message being shown as unreadable text in notifications, or offered for editing, copying, quoting or forwarding as text (iPhone, Android).
- Fixed Messages showing "Direct chat" instead of the other person's name for a moment.
- Fixed the "Calls can't reach this phone" notice staying on the keypad after the line had connected.
- Fixed importing a call flow that calls another flow: the called flow is now always created as a new one instead of reusing a same-named flow.
- Fixed the Mac app's update check sometimes reading the iPhone App Store listing instead of the Mac one (Mac).
- Fixed live updates (SMS status, chat, presence and live events) not reaching open screens on installations without the analytics database.
- Fixed the agent scheduling tabs running off the screen on a phone-width window (Admin, Contact centre, Scheduling).
- Fixed Android video calls: switching cameras mirrored the picture, video could stop when the app moved to the background, and camera errors were not reported (Android).
- Fixed the Mac app not asking for camera permission, so video calls had no picture (Mac).
- Fixed a crash when registering for push notifications on the Mac (Mac).
- Fixed repeated keychain password prompts after sign-in on the Mac (Mac).
- Fixed people added to a video room dropping out when the person who added them left.
- Fixed call flows with a Jira, Google Workspace, key-value, file storage, parcel tracking or ad conversion step failing to save.
- Fixed the password-reset e-mail sent through the MonoPbx mail relay containing only the link: it now includes the eight-digit code too.
- Fixed the `[auth]` section of the server configuration not being read, so the signed-in device limit can now be raised with `max_sessions_per_user` as documented.

## Security

- Security fixes (low): a regular user could trigger the application of a change set that the admin Copilot had proposed for an administrator. It is now refused before anything runs and the proposal stays available to the administrator.

**Jira steps for automations.** Create a Jira issue or add a comment from a flow, using the company's Jira connection (Admin, Jira).

**Salesforce, HubSpot and Pipedrive in automations.** These three CRMs can now be installed as integrations, so automations and AI agents can look up a caller and create contacts and notes in them (Admin, Settings, Integrations).
**Company key-value store for automations.** Three new steps keep and read small values (a counter, a last-seen date, a flag) across runs without setting up a table.

**Report ad conversions from a flow.** A flow can report a call as a Google Ads or Meta Ads conversion, using the same attribution and minimum talk-time rules as the automatic upload, and tells you why when nothing was sent.

**ConnectWise Manage and Autotask for managed-service providers.** The caller card shows the caller's company and open tickets, missed calls and voicemails can open a service ticket, and the partner portal can import PSA customers as client companies and export monthly usage per client (Admin, Settings, Integrations).

**Number reputation checks.** Look up whether a number is valid, its line type and carrier, and (with Twilio) a fraud-risk score, using your own Twilio Lookup or Numverify account. Use the answer in a flow, from an outbound-number monitor, or from a connected AI assistant (Admin, Settings, Integrations).
**Integration status.** Each integration now shows how far it has been checked against a real vendor account, and a new documentation page lists the status of every connector.

**Customer offboarding wizard for partners.** Hand a client company over in five steps: revoke devices, release numbers or mark them for port-out, record a final usage bill, and more. Each step is remembered and audited, nothing is ever deleted, and a legal hold blocks company deletion (Admin, Settings, System, Companies, Partners).

**MonoPhone for Mac updates itself.** The Mac app checks for updates daily and from Check for Updates in the app menu, the menu bar icon and Settings, shows what changed, and installs verified updates. Companies can turn it off with a device-management profile. The Mac app is now a signed, notarized drag-to-install disk image (Mac).

**Browser extension for Firefox.** Click-to-dial, the caller card and the phone panel (in the sidebar) now work in Firefox 140 or later, matching Chrome and Edge. Firefox for Android is not supported (Firefox).
**Message from your iPhone contacts.** On iPhone, Message on a contact card now offers MonoPhone, and you can ask Siri to send a message with MonoPhone (iPhone).

**Please note: sign-in limit.** When a user reaches the maximum number of signed-in devices, a new sign-in is now refused with a clear message instead of silently signing out their oldest device. The default limit is now 100 devices per user, and only devices used recently count. Users can sign out old devices from My devices.

**Please note: update the PBX for the newest app features.** Typing and last seen, per-member message info times, encrypted-chat quotes, the improved video rooms and Forgot password need this PBX release. Newer MonoPhone apps keep working for calls and chat with an older PBX.

Too many devices on a line: MonoPhone and the web console now say so plainly, explain that each installation counts as a device, and offer Remove an old device, after which the line connects (iPhone, Android, Mac, Windows, web console).

Recents in MonoPhone now combines this phone's own calls with the company call history, so a call missed seconds ago is always listed and counted, even when the history cannot be loaded. Names come from your contacts and the company phonebook, each day is shown once, and times use one format.

MonoPhone looks and feels more native on iPhone: system alerts, action sheets and menus, destructive actions in red, one empty-state style, coloured icon tiles on the Me page, clearer settings pages, and permission screens that explain each permission before the system asks for it, instead of a notification prompt right after sign-in.

MonoPhone on Android supports predictive back and a per-app language, uses Android wording in its settings, keeps live Quick Settings tiles and widget previews up to date, and goes Up to the right page after opening from a widget, tile or shortcut.

MonoPhone stays readable at large text sizes: the keypad fits above the tab bar on small phones, words and numbers no longer break mid-word, and Sign in stays reachable with the keyboard open on small phones.
When push notifications are not working, MonoPhone shows an amber notice that calls ring only while the app is open, instead of a general error (Android).

The call screen shows when the other side has put you on hold, offers only the controls that work while a call is ringing, explains when a video call has no camera, and shows a colleague's name instead of their extension.

Push-to-talk is more reliable: it notices a lost connection, reconnects at once when the network returns, rejoins your last channel after a restart, and keeps the last words of a transmission on Android.
Push-to-talk tells you when you are talking on your other device instead of dropping the audio silently.
Every page of the help documentation is now translated and kept current in all nine languages, and translated pages link correctly to their sections.

Automations that start from an integration event now cover more kinds of connectors, including ticketing, accounting, e-commerce, meetings and messaging. Orders from Amazon Mexico, Liverpool and Coppel are checked every 15 minutes and start those automations too.
The SMPP server can use a chosen certificate, reloads it without a restart, and checks that partner connections are still alive.
Notion gets a tool to append text to a page, usable from flows and AI assistants.
The automation "send webhook" step is now described as the way to trigger Zapier, Make and n8n.

A server address typed with the plain (non-secure) scheme in MonoPhone is now kept instead of silently switched to the secure one, with a clear warning on plain connections and the exact address named when it cannot be reached. An address typed without any scheme always uses the secure one (iPhone, Android, Mac, Windows).
Sending the onboarding invitation to a new device is much faster.
The call-flow designer can go full screen (a button in the zoom bar, or Ctrl or Cmd plus Shift plus F), and remembers your choice in that browser.
The automation "send SMS" step can send an MMS with picture or video links, on providers that support it (Twilio today).
The automation "post to Microsoft Teams" step posts to the channels of your Microsoft Teams integration.
The payment-link step lists only the payment connectors you have installed.
Automations can now start from an integration event only for a chosen record, for example a single order, using a field filter on the event.
The "add a note to the CRM" automation step no longer offers professional-services (PSA) and accounting connectors as if they were CRMs.
The automation "send email" step can set a reply-to address, so replies go to a person or shared mailbox instead of the sending address.
Maps follow the platform: Apple Watch shows Apple Maps, Android and Wear OS show Google Maps.
Video calls now prefer the more widely compatible video format, the same order audio already used.
When someone turns their camera off, their picture is replaced by their photo or initials and name.
The MonoPhone menu bar icon menu on the Mac is reorganized and shows the current version.
An SMS whose delivery result is unclear is now looked up before it is sent again.
On iPhone your own camera stays on in picture-in-picture during a video call or room, so the others still see you while you use another app, and your own picture appears in a small inset (iPhone).

Video rooms name every colleague on the tiles and in the room list, also in the web console when the colleague was dialled by number, and the web console's call header follows who is still in the room.

Add person in a video room no longer puts the room on hold while the new person's phone rings. When they cannot be reached, the room comes back at once and MonoPhone says why: busy, declined, cannot be reached, no answer, not found or not allowed (iPhone, Android).

German texts on Apple Watch and Wear OS now use the formal address like the rest of MonoPhone, and Spanish (Mexico) and Italian texts in the console, MonoPhone and the help documentation consistently use the informal address.
The integration status page now also lists HubSpot, Pipedrive, Salesforce, Numverify and Twilio Lookup, and eight help pages that could only be reached by a link now appear in the documentation menu.
Fixed attended transfer in MonoPhone: Transfer to your other call now works, and the transferred caller keeps their audio.
Fixed calling back from Recents or a contact card on iPhone, which did not place the call (iPhone).
Fixed push-to-talk being silent right after a voice or video call (iPhone, Android).
Fixed links from widgets, Quick Settings tiles, launcher shortcuts and app actions doing nothing on Android, including the push-to-talk tile (Android).
Fixed screen sharing crashing MonoPhone on Android 14 and later (Android).
Fixed the camera freezing when MonoPhone moved to the background during a video call; it now pauses and resumes (iPhone, Android).

Fixed chat problems: words typed while a message was being sent were lost, a chat left open in the background marked messages as read, a failed message disappeared instead of offering a retry, a deleted message came back while offline, the unread divider stayed put, and tapping a quote of an older message did nothing.
Fixed a message written offline showing the time it was finally sent instead of the time it was written.
Fixed an encrypted message being shown as unreadable text in notifications, or offered for editing, copying, quoting or forwarding as text (iPhone, Android).
Fixed Messages showing "Direct chat" instead of the other person's name for a moment.
Fixed the "Calls can't reach this phone" notice staying on the keypad after the line had connected.
Fixed importing a call flow that calls another flow: the called flow is now always created as a new one instead of reusing a same-named flow.
Fixed the Mac app's update check sometimes reading the iPhone App Store listing instead of the Mac one (Mac).
Fixed live updates (SMS status, chat, presence and live events) not reaching open screens on installations without the analytics database.
Fixed the agent scheduling tabs running off the screen on a phone-width window (Admin, Contact centre, Scheduling).
Fixed Android video calls: switching cameras mirrored the picture, video could stop when the app moved to the background, and camera errors were not reported (Android).
Fixed the Mac app not asking for camera permission, so video calls had no picture (Mac).
Fixed a crash when registering for push notifications on the Mac (Mac).
Fixed repeated keychain password prompts after sign-in on the Mac (Mac).
Fixed people added to a video room dropping out when the person who added them left.
Fixed call flows with a Jira, Google Workspace, key-value, file storage, parcel tracking or ad conversion step failing to save.
Fixed the password-reset e-mail sent through the MonoPbx mail relay containing only the link: it now includes the eight-digit code too.
Fixed the `[auth]` section of the server configuration not being read, so the signed-in device limit can now be raised with `max_sessions_per_user` as documented.

Security fixes (low): a regular user could trigger the application of a change set that the admin Copilot had proposed for an administrator. It is now refused before anything runs and the proposal stays available to the administrator.

notes.summary: Release 1.1: messaging on a par with the best chat apps, group video rooms with screen sharing on every device, sign-in on as many devices as you like, self-service password reset, a rebuilt push-to-talk, and new tools for automations, managed-service providers and AI oversight.
